title: Gender representation in highly cited endodontic research: A multivariate analysis
content:
by Esra Arılı Öztürk, Ceren Turan Gökduman, Şule Aktaş, Burhan Can Çanakçi

To evaluate the representation of women as first, last, and corresponding authors in highly cited endodontic articles and investigate factors related to female authorship. The 200 most-cited endodontic articles published between 2015 and 2024 were identified in the Web of Science Core Collection. Authors’ genders were determined using an automated database and manually verified. Associations between female authorship and journal features, geographic origin, funding, collaboration patterns, and citation performance were analyzed using multivariable regression models. Among 1,262 authors, 31% were women. Women represented 36% of first authors, 24.5% of last authors, and 33.5% of corresponding authors; 77.5% of articles included at least one woman. Female first authorship was more likely when the last or corresponding author was female. Funding was positively associated with female authorship, whereas author gender was not associated with citation counts. Women remain underrepresented in senior authorship positions in highly cited endodontic research.
